_meta.ward_variation_note: Segregation rules and collection schedules can vary across BBMP wards, residential welfare associations (RWAs), and gated communities. Please verify specific timings and dry waste collection center (DWCC) locations with your local ward BBMP office.

cardboard box.guidance: Flatten boxes and keep them dry. Hand over on dry waste collection days or to the local Dry Waste Collection Centre (DWCC).
cardboard box.edge_cases: If contaminated with food, grease, or oil (e.g., bottom of pizza boxes), cut off and compost/discard the greasy section in Wet Waste; recycle only the clean dry portions.

paper sheet.guidance: Keep clean and dry in your white/blue dry waste bag.
paper sheet.edge_cases: Shredded paper, wet paper, or tissue paper with bodily fluids cannot be recycled as paper (soiled tissue goes to sanitary waste).

newspaper.guidance: Bundle and keep dry. Highly valued for recycling and widely accepted by local raddiwala / DWCCs.
newspaper.edge_cases: Clean newspapers can also be reused to wrap sanitary waste before disposal. Do not include oiled or food-wrapped newspaper in paper recycling.

plastic bottle.guidance: Rinse clean, drain completely, and crush to save space in the dry waste bag.
plastic bottle.edge_cases: Remove beverage caps and rings if required by your local DWCC. Bottles with toxic chemicals must go to Domestic Hazardous Waste.

plastic bag.guidance: Clean, dry polythene bags go to Dry Waste collection. Karnataka has a ban on single-use plastic carry bags (<100 microns).
plastic bag.edge_cases: Dirty or food-stained bags must be rinsed and dried before bagging. Wet or decomposing food inside plastic bags contaminates entire dry waste batches.
plastic bag.source: BBMP Solid Waste Management Bye-laws 2020 (NEEDS VERIFICATION for micron threshold updates)

plastic wrapper.guidance: Clean wrappers and multilayer plastic packaging (MLP) go into the dry waste bag for DWCC collection.
plastic wrapper.edge_cases: Chips packets, biscuit wrappers, and laminated foils are non-recyclable via standard mechanical recycling but are collected in dry waste for coprocessing in cement kilns.
plastic wrapper.source: BBMP & Hasiru Dala Dry Waste Framework (NEEDS VERIFICATION)

plastic container.guidance: Wash out food residue, drain dry, and place in dry waste.
plastic container.edge_cases: Containers holding paints, motor oil, or pesticides must go to Domestic Hazardous Waste.

metal can.guidance: Rinse out food or beverage residues and place in the dry waste bin.
metal can.edge_cases: Be careful of sharp metal edges. Aerosol or pressurized spray cans must be placed with Domestic Hazardous Waste, NOT ordinary metal cans.

aluminium can.guidance: Rinse and crush. Recyclable infinitely through dry waste channels.
aluminium can.edge_cases: Do not mix with corrosive substances.

tin can.guidance: Rinse thoroughly to prevent attracting pests, then place in dry waste.
tin can.edge_cases: Fold sharp lid edges inwards to protect waste pickers from injury.

glass bottle.guidance: Rinse and keep intact. Place separately in dry waste or hand over carefully to waste collectors.
glass bottle.edge_cases: Broken glass must be carefully wrapped in thick newspaper or cardboard and labeled 'Broken Glass' to protect sanitation workers. Window glass and mirrors have different melting points and are treated as reject waste.

glass jar.guidance: Wash out pickles/sauces and place in dry waste or reuse at home for storage.
glass jar.edge_cases: Remove metal or plastic lids and sort each into its respective material category.

food waste.guidance: Place in the Green Bin (Wet Waste) without any plastic liner or bag. Collected daily by BBMP pourakarmikas for biomethanation or composting.
food waste.edge_cases: Never dispose of food waste inside plastic carry bags. Drain excessive gravies or soups before binning.

fruit peel.guidance: Directly into the Green Bin (Wet Waste) or home composting pit. Excellent organic compost material.
fruit peel.edge_cases: Remove fruit packaging stickers or plastic net packaging before disposal.

leaves.guidance: Garden and dry leaves should be composted locally or handed over with garden waste. Burning leaves is strictly prohibited and fined under BBMP bye-laws.
leaves.edge_cases: Large branches or landscaping bulk should not be dumped in daily wet bins; contact BBMP for bulk garden waste pickup.
leaves.source: BBMP Clean Air & SWM Bye-laws (NEEDS VERIFICATION)

battery.guidance: Do not throw in household wet or dry bins. Store dry in a sealed box and take to a designated e-waste drop-off bin or authorized recycler.
battery.edge_cases: Tape the terminals of lithium or button batteries with tape to prevent short circuits and fires in collection bins.

light bulb.guidance: CFLs and fluorescent tube lights contain toxic mercury vapour. Hand over carefully wrapped during hazardous/e-waste collection.
light bulb.edge_cases: If broken, ventilate the room for 15 minutes, sweep up using cardboard (do not vacuum), and seal in a plastic bag marked 'Mercury Hazard'.
light bulb.source: KSPCB Guidelines on Hazardous Household Waste (NEEDS VERIFICATION)

medicine.guidance: Expired or unused medicines must be kept in original packaging and handed over during BBMP domestic hazardous waste collection.
medicine.edge_cases: Never flush antibiotics, syrups, or pills down toilets or sinks, as they contaminate Bengaluru's groundwater and water bodies. Strip blister packaging if completely empty into dry waste.
medicine.source: Solid Waste Management Rules 2016 (NEEDS VERIFICATION for BBMP pharmacy return program)

syringe or needle.guidance: Sharps are an extreme biohazard and injury risk for waste workers. Place inside a puncture-proof plastic bottle or tin, cap it tightly, and label clearly 'SHARPS'.
syringe or needle.edge_cases: Never discard loose needles or recap used needles. Hand over separately to local clinics, pharmacies, or sanitary waste collectors.

medical waste.guidance: Bandages, cotton swabs, and dialysis kits must be wrapped securely in newspaper marked with a red cross (X) and handed to pourakarmikas as sanitary waste.
medical waste.edge_cases: Contaminated sharps must always follow the puncture-proof container protocol.
medical waste.source: BBMP 2-Bin 1-Bag Protocol (Red Bag / Red Cross Newspaper)

biohazard waste.guidance: Double wrap in leak-proof bags, mark with biohazard symbol or red cross, and hand over during domestic hazardous collection.
biohazard waste.edge_cases: Institutional biohazard waste requires licensed Common Bio-medical Waste Treatment Facility (CBWTF) pickup.

chemical container.guidance: Bottles of bleach, drain cleaners, and laboratory chemicals must be tightly sealed and disposed of as Domestic Hazardous Waste.
chemical container.edge_cases: Do not rinse corrosive chemicals into domestic sewage if they produce toxic fumes. Never mix leftover chemicals.

aerosol can.guidance: Pressurized cans can explode in compactor trucks or cause fires. Dispose with Domestic Hazardous Waste.
aerosol can.edge_cases: Never puncture or incinerate aerosol cans. Ensure completely depressurized if taking to metal scrap.
aerosol can.source: BBMP Domestic Hazardous Waste Guidelines (NEEDS VERIFICATION)

paint can.guidance: Paints, varnishes, and thinners contain toxic volatile compounds and heavy metals. Hand over on hazardous collection days.
paint can.edge_cases: Allow small residual paint quantities to dry completely into solid form before handing over; never pour liquid paint into drains or soil.

pesticide or poison.guidance: Insecticides, rat poisons, and garden pesticides are high-hazard toxic chemicals. Keep in original labeled container and hand to hazardous waste handlers.
pesticide or poison.edge_cases: Triple rinse empty pesticide bottles only if manufacturer instructions state so, and take empty containers to hazardous collection centres.
pesticide or poison.source: Insecticides Act / KSPCB Hazardous Waste Guidelines (NEEDS VERIFICATION)

other waste.guidance: If unsure, inspect the product material codes. Visit your ward's Dry Waste Collection Centre (DWCC) for advice.
other waste.edge_cases: Do not guess. Mixed composite materials (e.g., footwear, thermocol, mirrors) often require specialized reject waste routing.
